final_candidates.decision_summary: D473 (TM11) is the canonical cation-coordinating aspartate of OCT1; Asn is isosteric but charge-neutral, so the electrostatic substrate-binding determinant is deleted while helix packing, folding and abundance are preserved. Asn is essentially absent at this column among homologs and ESM-1v scores it highly implausible, consistent with functional ablation rather than tolerated variation.

R401 is the conserved arginine of the C-domain MFS A-motif (D397-R398-V399-G400-R401), whose salt-bridge network drives the rocker-switch alternating-access cycle; removing the charge blocks translocation. AlphaMissense scores it strongly pathogenic (0.892) with near-zero natural Ala frequency, and Ala is small and helix-compatible so the fold should remain intact.

Full side-chain and charge deletion at the same key binding aspartate, a classical loss-of-transport substitution in OCT homologs, with a strongly pathogenic AlphaMissense score (0.802). Ranked below D473N only because Ala is observed in ~13% of the (low-coverage) aligned homologs, slightly weakening the certainty of complete ablation.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence across phenotype, PLM and MSA dimensions is convergent and the only unused tool is static context-only, so further calls cannot change the final Top-3.

history.rationale: Position 473 (D in 'LCDIGGIITP') is the strictly conserved TM11 aspartate (UniProt D474) that provides the counter-charge for organic cation binding; Asn is isosteric and charge-neutralizing, so transport should be abolished with minimal folding/abundance cost.

D473 (canonical D474) is the conserved cation-binding aspartate of OCT1; the conservative D→N removes the charge without steric/packing disruption, so transport loss with preserved folding is most likely, and AlphaMissense still calls it pathogenic.

D473 (=Asp474 in Met-inclusive numbering) is the canonical cation-coordinating aspartate of OCT1 TM11; Asn is never seen at this position among homologs (freq 0) and ESM-1v judges it highly implausible, yet it is isosteric/neutral so folding and abundance should be preserved while cation binding is destroyed.

Trp216 (in 'GNWMAGY') lies in the large hydrophobic substrate-binding cleft (rOCT1 W218 equivalent) and is a key cation-pi contact; removal of the indole should eliminate substrate recognition while the membrane fold is retained.
Pathogenic AM class at a known cation-interaction tryptophan (rOCT1 W218 homolog); Trp→Ala carries some packing/folding risk, so it stays mid-pool.
Moderate AM (0.635) plus 9.5% natural Ala frequency at a well-covered column; deleting a large TM tryptophan also carries a packing/abundance risk, so it drops below the Ala-tolerant pocket mutants.

Arg174 in the MFS 'A-motif' (D170-R171-x-G173-R174-K175) mediates the salt-bridge network controlling rocker-switch conformational cycling; neutralizing it typically locks the transporter without preventing membrane insertion.
AM is only 'ambiguous' (0.460) for this A-motif arginine, weakening the LOF expectation; demoted.
N-domain A-motif Arg, but the AM score is ambiguous (0.460) which argues against full ablation; kept only as a low-ranked mechanistic backup.

Corresponds to the well-documented human OCT1 loss-of-function variant G401S in the TM8/TM9 region; small-to-polar substitution at a tightly packed glycine kills transport while the protein is still produced.
Ambiguous AM class (0.525) and a mild Gly→Ser change in the DRxGRR motif suggests possible partial retention of transport.
A-motif glycine, but AM is only borderline (0.525) and Ser occurs in 7.8% of homologs, so partial rather than complete transport loss is likely.
Tyr220 ('MAGYTLIT') aligns with rOCT1 Y222, a binding-pocket residue contacting cationic substrates; Ala truncation should abolish substrate coordination with modest structural perturbation.
High AM pathogenicity (0.756) at a TM4 substrate-cleft tyrosine (rOCT1 Y222 homolog) supports strong LOF; promoted above W216A.

Binding-cleft tyrosine (rOCT1 Y222 analogue) with solid AM (0.756), but Ala is observed at 4% of 185 aligned homologs, so complete ablation is less certain than for the A-motif/binding-Asp candidates.
Gln446 ('IAIQMICL') corresponds to rOCT1 Q448, a polar substrate-contacting residue in the inner cleft; loss of its side-chain hydrogen bonding is expected to prevent productive substrate binding.
Low/ambiguous AM (0.356) makes complete transport ablation improbable; dropped to free slots for stronger hypotheses.

rejection.reason: Low/ambiguous AM (0.356) makes complete transport ablation improbable; dropped to free slots for stronger hypotheses.

history.rationale: Thr224 (rOCT1 T226 equivalent) contributes a pocket hydroxyl for substrate/cation coordination; Ala is conservative in size and should be well tolerated structurally while impairing transport.
Clearly benign AM class (0.135) indicates the substitution is broadly tolerated and unlikely to abolish transport.

rejection.reason: Clearly benign AM class (0.135) indicates the substitution is broadly tolerated and unlikely to abolish transport.

history.rationale: Glu514 in the C-terminal MFS 'PETK' motif participates in the inter-domain charge network required for alternating access; charge-neutralizing substitution commonly yields expressed but transport-dead MFS carriers.
Only ambiguous AM (0.560) for the PETK-motif glutamate; conservative E→Q may be tolerated, so demoted to the tail of the pool.
Post-TM12 cytoplasmic position with only borderline AM (0.560) and the highest natural mutant frequency in the pool (Gln at 14% of homologs), making complete transport ablation unlikely.

rejection.reason: Post-TM12 cytoplasmic position with only borderline AM (0.560) and the highest natural mutant frequency in the pool (Gln at 14% of homologs), making complete transport ablation unlikely.

history.rationale: Phe158 (rOCT1 F160 equivalent, 'NAGFLF') is a binding-cleft aromatic; its removal should disrupt substrate stacking, though the cavity created may slightly reduce stability.
Strong AM signal (0.789) but the position is a buried TM2 aromatic where Ala truncation may destabilize rather than cleanly abolish transport, so only a modest promotion.

TM2 aromatic of the substrate cleft (equivalent to rOCT1 Phe160) with high AM (0.789) and very low ESM plausibility; the 9.5% natural Ala frequency at a well-covered column (app 0.87) tempers, but does not remove, the ablation hypothesis.

Matches the known human OCT1 loss-of-function polymorphism G465R in TM10; strongly LOF but carries a risk of reduced surface abundance, so it is ranked lower under the abundance-preserving constraint.

Top AM score (0.959) but that extremity likely reflects misfolding/destabilization of a TM glycine by a bulky charged Arg, which conflicts with the requirement to preserve abundance; kept but not promoted.

Highest AM (0.959) and zero natural Arg frequency, but burying a charged Arg in a TM helix is the classic way to destabilize/mistraffic a transporter, which violates the 'preserve abundance/folding' constraint; kept mid-pool rather than top.
Same key cation-binding aspartate as the top candidate but a fuller charge/side-chain deletion; Ala is small and helix-compatible, so folding should be preserved while binding is destroyed.

Full side-chain/charge deletion at the key binding Asp with a strong pathogenic AM score (0.802), but Ala occurs in 12.6% of the (low-coverage) homologs at this column, so it is slightly less certain than D473N as an absolute ablation.

R401 is the conserved arginine of the C-domain MFS A-motif (D397-R398-x-G400-R401); charge removal typically blocks the rocker-switch conformational cycle (transport) while the protein still folds and traffics.

R401 is the conserved Arg of the C-domain MFS A-motif (D397-R398-x-G400-R401) and AlphaMissense now scores it 0.892 (2nd highest) with near-zero natural Ala frequency; Ala is small and helix-compatible so the fold/abundance risk is low.
